tasks.short: Address a teaching issue with colleagues

steps.what: Read the teaching and research issues colleagues will address.
Collaborate with those colleagues on the teaching and research issues.

tasks.design: She reads the teaching and research issues, then meets the colleagues and addresses them in the room. No note is filed, no alert is raised, and no listing replaces the reading.
tasks.previous_blocker: The issue is between these colleagues, and only they know what was already tried.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new can settle a teaching or research issue in their place.
tasks.still_hard: The colleagues still have to agree, and a wrong stance is rework for the course.
tasks.human_edge: She can change her mind while the colleagues are talking.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still reads the issues and still meets the colleagues.

reach.task: align a teaching issue across a programme
reach.learn: The issue was settled in the meeting, not in a note.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: she still reads the issues and still collaborates with colleagues in the meeting. No tool is added.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
One episode is one meeting about one teaching or research issue. The colleagues are inside the organisation. The talk is spoken. No minute is filed, so the meeting is not gated.
She still opens and reads the issues. No listing replaces that reading. No alert is raised and nothing is sent.
unknowns: Whether this faculty expects a written minute of the meeting on another task.
research_questions: Who else must agree before a teaching issue can change a course.

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: One meeting about one teaching or research issue. She still reads the issues and still talks with the colleagues, so nothing is shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the current curricula, course content, materials, and methods.
Evaluate which methods of instruction to revise, and write the change notes.
Draft revised course materials that quote only her change notes.

loop.input: The change notes she wrote in s2. Each note names the curriculum section, the course content, the method of instruction she is changing, and an outcome sentence she copied from the current materials.
loop.output: Draft sections of course materials. Each section quotes one change note and adds no method she did not write.
loop.check: A section that does not quote a change note, or that adds a method or an outcome she did not write, is dropped. The loop does not judge whether the method is the right one to teach.
loop.stop: One pass. Dropped sections are not rewritten by the loop. If a note has no outcome sentence, that section is skipped. If every section is dropped, there is no draft and she writes the materials in the check.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot tell which method of instruction she decided to change on this course.

steps.what: Check the meaning of the course content against her change notes.
File the revised curricula and course materials as materials v1.

tasks.design: She reads the current curricula and writes change notes that name the content and the method of instruction she is changing. A loop drafts course materials by quoting only those notes. She checks the meaning of every section, then files materials v1 on the {LMS} herself. No listing replaces the reading, and nothing is sent to a student.
tasks.previous_blocker: The method of instruction is a judgement about this course, so a blank template invents changes she did not choose.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can quote only the change notes she wrote, and drop a section that adds a method she did not write.
tasks.still_hard: A new curriculum, or a change in what is safe to teach, still needs her rewrite.
tasks.human_edge: She decides which content and which method of instruction change.

ambition.what: On every revision she states which method of instruction changes, including a small content fix, before any draft is written.

tasks.altitude: She still reads the current materials, still decides the changes, still checks every section, and still files materials v1. The week loses only the first composition of text she already decided.

reach.learn: The methods of instruction are the ones she filed as materials v1, after she checked them.

evidence.claim: In a University of Michigan trial, assistants agreed with 88 percent of AI judgments on student essays. The report gives no time data.

That trial is essay feedback, not a revision of curricula or methods of instruction. The 88 percent is not used as hours saved on this task. Model knowledge: she still reads and rewrites the course materials.
Annex III point 3 covers evaluating learning outcomes, admission, and detecting cheating in tests. This draft does not evaluate a learner or set a grade.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results, and only the board sanctions fraud. This task files course materials and does not set a result.

assumptions: She produces the change notes in s2 before any draft. Each note names the curriculum section, the course content, the method of instruction she is changing, and an outcome sentence copied from the current materials. If a note has no outcome sentence, the loop skips that section and she writes it during the check.
The current materials already stand in the {DOCS}. She still opens and reads them in s1. No listing replaces that reading. The loop may quote only sentences she copied into the change notes.
One hour per 100 baseline hours is retiring a change note so a later run does not quote a method she has dropped. Her reading and rewrite on this run sit in the check and are not deducted again.

The 12-point draft share is the first composition of text she already decided. The 28-point check is her reading every section and rewriting what is wrong. She files materials v1 herself. No grade is set, nothing is sent to a student, and no alert is raised.
Essay-feedback trials and grading-time reports are not used as hours.
unknowns: Whether this faculty also requires a programme-director sign-off before the learning system accepts materials v1.
Whether logging the drafts would count as staff monitoring under national rules.
research_questions: How often she rejects the whole draft and writes the materials herself.

already_counted.description: Reading every drafted section and rewriting the course content that does not match her change notes.

incremental.description: Retiring a change note so a later run does not quote a method of instruction she has dropped.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: One revision of one course. Low is a sitting where she rejects the draft and writes the materials during the check, so nothing is saved. High is the 12-point first composition minus 1 hour per 100 baseline hours for retiring old change notes. She still reads the current materials, still checks every section, and still files materials v1. Essay-feedback trials and grading-time reports are not used.

steps.what: Maintain the regularly scheduled office hours and listen.
Advise and assist the students during those office hours.

tasks.design: She maintains the regularly scheduled office hours, listens, and advises the students in the room. No version of the advice is written or sent, and no listing replaces the hour.
tasks.previous_blocker: The student arrives with a problem she has not seen.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new can advise or assist the student in her place.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong steer during the hour can set the student back.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the student and changes the help while they are in the room.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still holds the office hours and still advises the students herself.

reach.learn: The help was spoken with the student during the hour.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: she still listens and still advises the students during the office hours. No tool is added.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
One episode is one block of regularly scheduled office hours. The student is outside the organisation. The help is spoken in the room. No version is written or sent, so the hour is not gated.
No listing replaces the hour. No alert is raised and nothing is sent.
unknowns: Whether a written note of the office-hour help sits on another task.
research_questions: Who covers the office hours when she is away.

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: One block of office hours. She still listens and still advises the students, so nothing is shortened.

steps.what: Read the academic and vocational curricula the students ask about.
Decide the career issues those students are facing.
Advise the students on those curricula and career issues.

tasks.design: She reads the academic and vocational curricula, decides the career issues, and advises the students herself. No draft is sent to the student, and no listing replaces the reading.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right path depends on this student's situation, which is not a rule.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new can tell the student which curriculum or career to choose.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong career steer is hard to undo.
tasks.human_edge: She can weigh the student's situation while she is talking to them.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still reads the curricula and still advises the students herself.

reach.task: advise a learner on a vocational path
reach.learn: The career advice was spoken to the student, after she had read the curricula.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: she still reads the curricula and still advises the students on career issues. No tool is added.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.

One episode is one conversation with one student about academic or vocational curricula and career issues. The student is outside the organisation. The advice is spoken. No version is written or sent, so the conversation is not gated.
She still opens and reads the curricula. No listing replaces that reading. No alert is raised and no draft is sent.
unknowns: Whether a written record of the career advice sits on another task.
research_questions: Which curriculum rules only the faculty office can confirm.

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: One conversation with one student about curricula and career issues. She still reads the curricula and still gives the advice, so nothing is shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still meets colleagues about teaching and research issues, still evaluates and files the curricula, still holds office hours, and still advises students. The draft does not decide what to teach.
reach: An instructional coordinator learns a teaching issue was settled in the meeting.
An instructional coordinator learns the methods of instruction are the ones she filed as materials v1.
A tutor learns the office-hour help was spoken with the student.
A career and technical education teacher learns the career advice was spoken to the student.
skills_to_grow: Settle a teaching or research issue with the colleagues in the room.
Write change notes before any draft of course materials.
Advise the student during the office hour.
Tell the student the career advice herself.
role.ambitious_version: The same teacher still holds the meetings, the office hours, and the career conversations, and she still files the curricula. A draft only composes text she already decided.
